slides: Focus and coherence.
Two of the easiest places to lose points... and two of the easiest to fix.
Focus is how short and precise our text is. No repetition, no padding. We write exactly what we want, and we don't ramble.
Coherence is the line of thought. Everything is clear. There's a clear link between the ideas, between the sentences, between the parts of sentences. No jumping from topic to topic.
Let's look at some examples.
Read this paragraph.
It's long, isn't it? It looks rich. So let's go through it again, and look for the repetition and the padding.
First, words that repeat.
Public spaces, public spaces, public spaces. Offence, offence, offence. Break the law, break the law.
That's not good, and you know it from the language lessons. We fix it with pronouns, and by saying it in other words.
But the problem here goes beyond repeated words. The repetition is in the ideas.
So let's mark the sentences by idea.
'Unequivocal' and 'beyond any doubt'. It's the same thing. Repeating it doesn't really stress anything. It's just repetition.
Deter citizens from breaking the law. Afraid to commit the offence because he might be caught. Deter offenders in case they are caught. It's the same idea, in three colours.
Reduce crime, avoid committing the offence, fewer crimes. The same result, again and again.
It looks long and rich, but really it's about one and a half sentences, repeated in different words. No real development.
And this sentence.
We don't need all this detail. It's padding. It's only there to make the paragraph bigger. It tells us nothing new.
So that's the whole idea of focus. Be short and to the point. Don't go back to the same idea again and again, in other words or another wording.
So what should you do?
It's better to write a shorter paragraph that's focused and to the point.
Even if it isn't perfect, even if you feel your development isn't good enough... at least you won't lose extra points for repetition and padding.
Need more lines? Add a new step to the explanation. Not the same step again.
This paragraph gets a big X for repetition and padding.
Now, coherence. The line of thought. Read this one.
Did you notice? Even I got stuck reading it. It's hard to read. There are jumps. There's no clear line of thought.
Each sentence on its own is fine. But they're not connected to each other. So let's fix it.
Sentence one. Installing the cameras is a desirable step. Why? Why is it desirable?
Because it can reduce crime. So we join them with 'since', a connector of explanation. The second part explains the first.
And we also drop the repeated 'installing face-recognition cameras in public spaces'. We just say 'it'.
Next, the public will benefit. How is that connected? Well, it's the result. We reduced crime, and that leads to the public benefiting.
So we add 'consequently'. And instead of 'public spaces' yet again, we write 'the monitored areas'.
Next sentence. The justice system will work more efficiently.
That's another advantage. Another reason it's desirable. So, 'In addition'. And 'the cameras', not 'the identification cameras' again. 'Those who broke the law', not 'in public spaces' again.
Last sentence. Is it connected to the justice system? No. It's one more advantage. Deterrence.
I already used 'in addition', so I change it. 'Moreover'. And 'a person', not 'a criminal'. He isn't a criminal yet.
We didn't make this paragraph perfect. But the line of thought is now much clearer.
A desirable step, since it reduces crime. Consequently, the public benefits. In addition, the justice system. Moreover, deterrence.
Yes, 'public spaces' repeats again. But now we're looking for a different problem.
The first part is positive. Fewer crimes. Then 'Likewise', a connector of addition. And the second part is negative. Harm to privacy.
So the link between the parts is wrong. We need contrast. 'However', 'On the other hand'. And that's also a break in the line of thought.
So when you proofread, do two checks. Does each sentence add something new? And does the connector show the real relationship?
That's focus and coherence. See you in the next lesson, on critical thinking.
